angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 603,868 km at 49.74 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: distance 49.743 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 49.743 +/- 0.597 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 20.2837 +/- 0.0167 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05), 1214.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.868 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: radius 0.868 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.364 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.053) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 603,868 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4814 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: effective temperature 4814 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.059) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: effective temperature 4814 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.059) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of BD+14 4559 (pscomppars): spectral type K2 V, from Niedzielski et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...707..768N/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of BD+14 4559 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.17 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of BD+14 4559 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.32, from Niedzielski et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...707..768N/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of BD+14 4559 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.5 km/s, from Niedzielski et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...707..768N/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.9 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 6 published values span log g 4.03 to 4.9, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.5% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
